_comment: Internal counsel intake facts and unresolved questions. Scripts refresh hashes only; supplied reviews, decisions and receipts are never invented or overwritten.
jurisdictionAssumption: US-first planning; intended markets and actual filing jurisdictions require owner and counsel decisions.

candidates.title: Athlete-tagged Highlights and changing privacy permissions
candidates.problem: A Highlight can identify an athlete while audience, approval or block state changes. Review how displayed identity and access remain consistent across those changes.
candidates.baseline: Tagged media and audience controls are established patterns. No prior-art search or measured comparative baseline has been completed for this candidate.
candidates.mechanism: Investigate the implemented request/approval and feed-reading sequence across the Highlights and privacy SDKs and canonical SQL. Engineering must trace exact states, denied actors and revocation behavior before proposing a technical distinction.
candidates.alternatives: Compare ordinary access checks, feed-time identity filtering and approval-based tagging. These are investigation options, not documented search results.
candidates.limitations: Source references establish a reading scope only. Current hosted behavior, novelty, inventorship and claim scope are unverified.
candidates.humanContributions: Unknown: collect specific human conception/authorship, dates, AI involvement and assignment evidence from the owner and contributors.
counselQuestions: Is there a precise qualifying technical contribution beyond familiar tagged-media and privacy techniques?
Which states/steps and evidence would support a useful claim or justify keeping know-how confidential?

candidates.title: Private media entitlement and access revocation
candidates.problem: Private media must remain restricted as entitlements and permissions change. Review the boundary between client references, trusted authorization and delivery.
candidates.baseline: Entitlements, signed media access and revocation are established techniques. No novelty or freedom-to-operate study has been performed.
candidates.mechanism: Trace Vault SDK requests and canonical database permissions, then compare provider-neutral media references with private access enforcement. Identify actual denial/revocation behavior and legacy gaps rather than treating a UI lock as authorization.
candidates.alternatives: Compare short-lived signed URLs, trusted streaming authorization and entitlement checks; provider-specific behavior requires separate evidence.
candidates.limitations: Legacy/public-byte and hosted authorization boundaries require current source and environment review. No patentability, rights or production-security conclusion is recorded.
candidates.humanContributions: Unknown: obtain human contribution dates, AI-assisted work history, employer/contract context and assignments.
counselQuestions: Does any verified mechanism differ meaningfully from existing entitlement and private-media systems?
What technical disclosure and commercially relevant claim scope would justify a filing?

candidates.title: Live-score event reconciliation and reconnect behavior
candidates.problem: A sideline score display can receive delayed or conflicting events and reconnect after losing a connection. Review the merge/refetch decisions and resulting score consistency.
candidates.baseline: Event ordering, duplicate handling and reconnect reconciliation are common distributed-system patterns. A comparative performance/correctness baseline and prior-art search are absent.
candidates.mechanism: Trace the per-game Broadcast merge/refetch helper into the live-score hook and canonical SQL. Document exact inputs, ordering assumptions, fallback requests and failure cases; identify which paths are behind a default-off switch.
candidates.alternatives: Compare refetch-only updates, sequence-based reconciliation and event replay. Test relevant duplicates, reorderings and reconnects before claiming improvements.
candidates.limitations: Local source and disabled switches do not establish deployed behavior or technical novelty. Engineering must supply current test and hosted evidence where relevant.
candidates.humanContributions: Unknown: collect human conception and implementation contributions, dates, AI usage and ownership records.
counselQuestions: Is any demonstrated reconciliation method eligible, new and non-obvious relative to prior event-sync systems?
What actual evidence distinguishes technical benefit from ordinary use of the provider SDK?

rightsChecklist.needed: Human authorship, creation/publication dates, work versions, claimant and signed assignment/employment records; counsel selects registration and deposits.
Specific human/AI contributions and tool terms; counsel evaluates eligible authorship, inventorship and any excluded material.
License/notice audit against the exact lockfile, upstream patches, examples and provider terms; manifests alone do not prove compliance.

rightsChecklist.category: GUI, logo, fonts, icons, art and sound
rightsChecklist.needed: Creator/license evidence, stable originals and design history; counsel assesses copyright/design-patent scope and trademark clearance.
Contributor roles, specific human contributions and counsel-reviewed signed assignments or licenses; Git names are not inventorship proof.
Actual permissions/licenses for footage, photos, music and school/provider marks; user content is not automatically company IP.
Owner-approved private storage, actual repository/provider access review, confidentiality agreements and disclosure/patent-publication choices.

disclosureEvents.summary: Owner reports nothing has been made public. This is not an independently verified audit; counsel must check earlier sharing, sales/offers and intended launch dates.
disclosureEvents.evidence: Owner reply in the current IP planning conversation, 2026-10-22; actual repository visibility and historical events unverified.

counselQuestions: Which jurisdictions, deadlines and searches should be prioritized before public disclosure?
Which human authors/inventors and assignment documents are required for this AI-assisted project?
Which works, exclusions, registration groups and safe deposits fit copyright protection?
Which candidates warrant a patent search, provisional/full filing, trade-secret treatment or a documented decision to decline?
What trademark clearance, original GUI design review and separate freedom-to-operate scope are justified?
What engagement fees, filing/response costs, actual docket ownership and approved sharing controls are required?
